the Triton kernel, TTIR
levels.produced_by: Not the specimen. A cited public capture of the nearest neighbour: lines 6-73 of test/TritonGPU/matmul.mlir in triton-lang/triton at tag v3.7.1, commit f797708c0626e5f9840ca5b0a98790e2c7cb09ad, copied verbatim. It is a blocked f32 matmul, 64x64 tiles over a 64-deep k loop, carrying the Triton frontend's specialization mangling in its name. The file's lit RUN line compiles it for cuda:80, so Ampere. It is a matmul and not an attention block, and its tiles are 64x64x64 against the specimen's 16x32. Tensors carry no layout encoding, which is what TTIR is.

levels.title: the Triton kernel, TTGIR
levels.produced_by: Not the specimen. A cited public capture of the nearest neighbour: lines 66-163 of test/TritonGPU/loop-pipeline-cuda.mlir in triton-lang/triton at tag v3.7.1, commit f797708c0626e5f9840ca5b0a98790e2c7cb09ad, copied verbatim. One complete module for _jagged_hstu_attn_fwd_0d1d2d3d4d5de, the forward kernel of Meta's jagged HSTU attention, with two chained dots and every tensor type now carrying a layout: #blocked for the thread mapping, #ttg.nvidia_mma for the accumulator, #ttg.swizzled_shared for the staging buffers, #ttg.dot_op for the operands. It is attention but not this attention: ragged sequences, persistent tiling, and no softmax between the two dots in this reduced test input. The module declares four warps and one CTA; the nvidia_mma layout is version 2 with instrShape [16, 8], which is the Ampere-era mma, but the module carries no ttg.target string, so the sm number is not stated by the source.

A cuobjdump listing of warp_mma_16x16x16, mangled _Z17warp_mma_16x16x16P6__halfS0_Pf, whose twenty-line CUDA source is committed beside it: three nvcuda::wmma fragments at 16x16x16, half operands with a float accumulator, one load_matrix_sync each, one mma_sync, one store_matrix_sync. The listing names its own generation, arch = sm_80 with headerflags EF_CUDA_SM80, so Ampere; it does not name the nvcc that produced it.
